newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Empire soars on denial of bankruptcy rumour.
newsitem.headline: Empire soars on denial of bankruptcy rumour.

text.p: Empire East Land Holdings Inc gained 85 centavos, or 23.29 percent in early trade to 4.50 pesos on Wednesday after the company and a senior government official denied it was in serious financial difficulty, brokers said.

"The company said that rumours that they are filing for bankruptcy are not true and coupled with positive sentiment in the market, it boosted the stock," said Alexis Cabel, analyst at Angping & Associates Securities.

Empire was the most heavily traded stock in early trade with turnover worth 126.86 million pesos. Its parent company, Megaworld Properties & Holdings Inc also posted early gains of 75 centavos, or 20 percent, to 4.50 pesos.
"Their rise is on news denying that they were cash-strapped. Investors are going back and taking advantage of their low prices," said Lawrence de Leon, analyst at Dharmala Securities.
Central Bank deputy governor Alberto Reyes told Reuters that the outstanding loans of both companies were in order when the bank conducted a check in the midst of the rumours.
Talks of bankruptcy battered both Empire and Megaworld stocks on Tuesday. Empire posted a record low close of 3.65 pesos while Megaworld ended at a year low close of 3.75 pesos.
